prediction_ref.short_label: Local-LLM runtimes ship in-model speculative decoding on by default by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Today's Ollama release is the origin evidence for this fresh prediction. Ollama shipped version 0.31 on July 1 with multi-token prediction enabled by default for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon, and reports the model generating tokens nearly 90% faster on average across a coding-agent benchmark with byte-identical output. The mechanism is in-model speculative decoding: Gemma 4 bundles a small draft model that proposes several next tokens and the main model verifies them in one pass, so multiple tokens land for roughly the cost of one when the draft is accepted. Crucially this ships as a default rather than a tuning flag, and the small-batch MLX matmul kernel Ollama upstreamed, which makes Gemma 4's largest matmuls 2x-2.5x faster on an M5 Max with nvfp4, is reusable by any MLX model rather than just Gemma. That is exactly the one-shipping-implementation-proves-the-accuracy-neutral-speedup dynamic this prediction expects to spread, and because coding agents call the model continuously over highly predictable text, accepted drafts compound over a session. What is still missing is a second mainstream local runtime, LM Studio, an llama.cpp desktop, MLX-LM, or vLLM's local mode, flipping in-model or paired-draft speculative decoding to the default path for a popular open-weight family.
